message.content:
Civil law, also known as civil jurisprudence or civil law system, is a legal framework that governs non-criminal disputes between private parties. Its components can be broadly categorized into several key areas: | Component | Description | |-----------|-------------| | **Sources of Law** | • **Statutes & Codes** – Written laws enacted by legislatures (e.g., Civil Code, Commercial Code).
• **Case Law / Precedent** – Judicial decisions that interpret statutes and establish common‑law principles.
• **Custom & Practice** – Long‑standing local customs that may be recognized by courts. | | **Legal Subjects** | • **Persons** – Natural persons, legal entities (companies, NGOs).
• **Property** – Real property, movable property, intellectual property.
• **Contracts** – Agreements, obligations, performance, breach.
• **Torts** – Wrongful acts causing harm or loss.
• **Family Law** – Marriage, divorce, child custody, inheritance. | | **Procedural Elements** | • **Jurisdiction** – Which court has authority over a case.
• **Venue** – Physical location where a case is heard.
• **Pleadings** – Complaint, answer, counterclaim, etc.
• **Evidence Rules** – Admissibility, burden of proof.
• **Remedies** – Damages, injunctions, specific performance. | | **Legal Principles** | • **Doctrine of Res Judicata** – Finality of judgments.
• **Doctrine of Estoppel** – Preventing contradictory claims.
• **Doctrine of Good Faith** – Parties must act honestly. | | **Specialized Areas** | • **Commercial Law** – Business contracts, corporate governance.
• **Consumer Protection** – Rights of buyers, product liability.
• **Environmental Law** – Property rights, pollution liability. | | **Enforcement Mechanisms** | • **Judicial Enforcement** – Court orders, writs.
• **Administrative Enforcement** – Regulatory agencies, licensing boards.
• **Alternative Dispute Resolution** – Mediation, arbitration. | These components interact to form a comprehensive system that resolves disputes, protects rights, and promotes fairness in civil society.
